title: Polysome Profiling in Primary Differentiating Murine Adipocytes
author: De Siqueira, Nouhi, et al.

steps.title: Collect adipose tissue pads
steps.instruction: Using sterile scissors and forceps, excise epididymal (eWAT) and inguinal (iWAT) fat pads from mice, place whole pads in cold PBS containing 1 % Penicillin‑Streptomycin, and remove lymph nodes from iWAT with sterile forceps.

steps.title: Mince tissue and add digestion media
steps.instruction: Mince 2–3 g of the adipose pads in a sterile 6‑well plate with 1 mL digestion media (DMEM + 1 % BSA + 1 mg/mL type II collagenase) using sharp scissors for 2–3 min, then add an additional 3 mL digestion media.

steps.title: Digest tissue at 37°C
steps.instruction: Incubate the minced tissue for 30 min at 37 °C with agitation at 120 rpm, pipetting the suspension up and down every 15 min to aid dissociation.

steps.title: Stop digestion and filter suspension
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 2 mM EDTA in DMEM to stop digestion, transfer the mixture to a 50 mL tube, then add 30 mL of DMEM containing 1 % Pen/Strep to a new tube fitted with a 100 µm cell strainer (pre‑wetted with 1 mL 1 % Pen/Strep DMEM) and filter the suspension using circular motions to avoid clogging.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash cell pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension for 10 min at 700 × g at 4 °C, carefully aspirate the fat layer and supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL 1 % Pen/Strep DMEM, add 9 mL fresh DMEM, and pass the cells through a pre‑wetted 40 µm cell strainer.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and resuspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the strained cells for 3 min at 700 × g at 4 °C, then resuspend the pellet in 1 mL complete DMEM (10 % FBS, 1 % Pen/Strep, 50 µg/mL Primocin).

steps.title: Plate and expand primary adipocytes
steps.instruction: Plate the cells in a 15‑cm dish with 25 mL complete DMEM, incubate overnight, wash twice the next day with warm 1 % Pen/Strep PBS to remove red blood cells and debris, add fresh complete DMEM, and culture until ~80 % confluency, changing media every 2 days (use only one passage).

steps.title: Refresh media before polysome profiling
steps.instruction: Replace the maintenance medium with fresh complete DMEM and incubate the cells for 1 h to boost translation.

steps.title: Cycloheximide treatment and washes
steps.instruction: Treat cells with 100 µg/mL cycloheximide for 5 min at 37 °C, then wash twice with ice‑cold PBS containing 100 µg/mL cycloheximide.

steps.title: Hypotonic lysis and cell scraping
steps.instruction: Add 540 µL hypotonic buffer (5 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1.5 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 100 µg/mL cycloheximide, 1 mM DTT, 1× protease inhibitor, 200 U/mL RNase inhibitor, RNase‑free water) directly to the plate, scrape cells with a cell scraper, tilt plates 45° on ice, pipette up/down twice to resuspend, transfer the suspension to a cold 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and note the estimated volume (EV).

steps.title: Add detergents and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube for 5 s, then add 5 % of EV volume of 10 % Triton‑X‑100 and 5 % of EV volume of 10 % sodium deoxycholate, vortex another 5 s, and centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 7 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect supernatant and store input
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared supernatant to a new pre‑chilled 1.5 mL tube, measure OD₂₆₀, keep 10 % of the lysate (≈50 µL) as input, add 450 µL ddH₂O and 500 µL TRIzol LS to the input, and store at –80 °C (desired lysate OD₂₆₀ between 10 and 20).

steps.title: Load lysate onto sucrose gradients
steps.instruction: Remove 500 µL from the top of each pre‑formed sucrose gradient, then slowly layer 450 µL of the cell lysate on top, taking care not to disturb the gradient.

steps.title: Balance tubes and ultracentrifuge
steps.instruction: Weigh and balance the gradient tubes using hypotonic lysis buffer, then centrifuge at ~160,000 × g (36,000 RPM) for 2 h at 4 °C in an SW41Ti rotor with no brake and zero acceleration/deceleration.

steps.title: RNA extraction from gradients
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from the gradient fractions (e.g., using TRIzol LS as described) and store at –80 °C until library preparation.

steps.title: FastQC quality control
steps.instruction: Run FastQC with default parameters on raw sequencing reads from both total‑RNA and polysome‑associated samples.

steps.title: Map reads with Salmon
steps.instruction: Map the sequencing reads to the mouse reference genome (mm10) using Salmon.

steps.title: DESeq2 differential expression (total & polysome)
steps.instruction: Perform differential gene expression analysis separately on total‑RNA and polysome data with DESeq2, defining significant DEGs as those with adjusted p‑value ≤ 0.2.

steps.title: Compare DEGs with Fisher test
steps.instruction: Compare the DEG lists from total‑RNA and polysome analyses using Fisher’s Exact Test; overlapping DEGs represent tightly coupled transcription‑translation regulation.

steps.title: Interaction DESeq2 model for DTETs
steps.instruction: Include an interaction term between RNA fraction (polysome vs total) and treatment (Rosiglitazone vs vehicle) in a DESeq2 model to identify differentially translated transcripts (DTETs) using adjusted p‑value ≤ 1.

steps.title: Extract sequences and scan hexamers
steps.instruction: Extract 5′‑UTR, coding, and 3′‑UTR sequences of DTETs based on GENCODE VM33 annotations, then slide a 6‑nt window (step 1 nt) across each transcript to record overlapping hexamers.

steps.title: Hexamer enrichment and motif analysis
steps.instruction: Count hexamer occurrences, compute enrichment scores with a Z‑test, retain hexamers with enrichment Z‑score > 3, and perform motif analysis using RSAT and ggseqlogo to generate sequence logos.

description: It would be helpful to work with stable cell lines before optimizing the protocol for primary cells. A cell line with a similar phenotype would be ideal to first test the yield of RNA after lysis in the hypotonic buffer and to assess the quality of the polysome profile. In our case, we performed troubleshooting with 10T1/2 cells before isolating the stromal vascular fraction. In addition to that, if using primary cells from mice an approved animal use protocol will also be necessary.
